decisions.quote: In the replication study (RQs 1–3), we find largely consistent experimental effects to the original RCT, where having access to the recommendation lists led to the recruit- ment of substantially more instructionally effective and experienced CMs. Across both years of implementation, PSTs assigned to treatment mentors reported feeling signifi- cantly more prepared to teach. Notably, Cohort 2 effects were about half the magnitude as those for Cohort 1 and not statistically significant; however, as we administered the survey for Cohort 2 in the spring of 2020 during the first wave of the COVID pandemic, PSTs were faced with much uncertainty and often had to move to online instruction, which may explain some of these between-cohort differences.
decisions.location: Introduction, p. 4, lines 180-188 (see also Results, p. 15, lines 734-739)
decisions.reason: The replication confirmed the original study's finding that recommendation lists led to recruiting more instructionally effective and experienced clinical mentors (both in Cohort 2 and the three-program extension), but explicitly contrasted the replication cohort's smaller, statistically nonsignificant effect on preservice teachers' feelings of preparedness to teach with the original RCT.

parent_objection: The first review selects mixed from a smaller, nonsignificant positive preparedness effect in Cohort2 versus the original Cohort1, while the paper says: In the replication study(RQs1–3),we find largely consistent experimental effects to the original RCT. The codebook gives an authors overall verdict priority and says a smaller/weaker effect treated as supported is successful; own statistical significance is not the outcome. Determine whether this is an overall replication verdict or only confirmation of mentor-recruitment outcomes, and whether authors explicitly treat preparedness as an original finding that failed rather than an imprecise same-direction difference. Inspect the full results/discussion. OriginalCohort1 pooled data cannot substitute for the new Cohort2 outcome. New clinical-assessment/workforce outcomes and multi-program extension must not be misread as original findings. Final category must follow authors own scope and comparisons,not parent preferred p-value rule. The original Ronfeldt2020 identity is settled. This is the second and final call,including mechanical retries.

shipped.title_o: Improving Preservice Teachers’ Feelings of Preparedness to Teach Through Recruitment of Instructionally Effective and Experienced Cooperating Teachers: A Randomized Experiment
shipped.authors_o: Ronfeldt; Bardelli; Truwit; Mullman; Schaaf; Baker
shipped.outcome_quote: we replicate the previous study with a second cohort, finding again that the initiative led to the recruitment of more instructionally effective and experienced mentors.

blind_target.authors: Ronfeldt, M., Bardelli, E., Truwit, M., Mullman, H., Schaaf, K., & Baker, J. C.
blind_target.title: Improving preservice teachers’ feelings of preparedness to teach through recruitment of instructionally effective and experienced cooperating teachers: A randomized experiment
blind_target.evidence_quote: In this paper, we describe a pair of studies that build upon the “original” MMR evalu- ation (Ronfeldt et al., 2020) in two different ways. In the “replication study,” we re-imple- ment the original experiment (Cohort 1, 2018–19) with a different cohort of PSTs and CMs within the same EPP (Cohort 2, 2019–20).
blind_target.outcome_quote: First, across years, PSTs who completed their clinical placements in treated districts reported feeling more ready to teach than their peers in control districts. These results are consistent for the overall feelings of readiness factor and its twosub-factors, readiness in questioning skills and readiness in other instruc- tional skills. Compared to the original RCT, though, these differences are smaller in magnitude and not statistically significant in the replication study.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Mentor recruitment effects supported in new cohorts, but authors explicitly contrast nonsignificant readiness effects with the original RCT. Successful mentor recruitment addresses that component rather than all tested findings. New clinical assessment and workforce measures are extensions. Quote shows explicit contrary comparison; recruitment agreement is stated in results and discussion.
